baselines.name: Random bot
baselines.what_it_is: Frankie's body. Each tick it picks an action at random from the legal actions and eats or skips at random. Gives the chance level. Ledger X03.

baselines.name: Lookup-table bot
baselines.what_it_is: Stores the exact trait values and outcome of every item it eats. It eats exact matches of good items and skips exact matches of bad ones, and handles anything else by the rule in its frozen spec. Brute memory with no generalising. Ledger X03.

baselines.name: Nearest-neighbour eat/skip bot
baselines.what_it_is: The ledger X03 version: a standalone bot for probes, with no drive and no tower. It stores every eaten item separately, so it splits on any difference. For a new object it finds the nearest stored item over all traits, weighted equally, and eats if that item was good, skips if it was bad, and tries the object if memory is empty. Used where a test scores single eat/skip responses. Ledger X36.

baselines.name: Nearest-neighbour forager
baselines.what_it_is: B1n-bot's eat/skip memory placed on Frankie's body, plus B4's greedy movement: it walks to the nearest object in view that its memory does not mark as bad, and does a random walk when none is in view. It has no drive, no reserve, no habits and no proposal menu. This is the floor that C7 called 'B1n' without defining it. Ledger X36.

baselines.name: Frankie with nearest-neighbour memory
baselines.what_it_is: Frankie's body, drive, reserve, untried-value rule, proposal menu, randomness curve and habit rule, with the recognition tower, candidate memory and write rule replaced by a nearest-neighbour memory of each eaten item. Everything else is unchanged, so it is the honest 'bad elimination' bar. C3's B1n and C13's 'B1n-mind' are one shared definition. Ledger X36.

baselines.name: Sequence keep-and-retry learner
baselines.what_it_is: Frankie's body, proposal menu and designed greedy movement rule. It keeps and retries any action sequence that paid, and otherwise draws again from the menu. It decides eat/skip with B1n-bot's nearest-neighbour memory. Brute trial and error on Frankie's own menu. Ledger X36.

baselines.name: Surface matcher
baselines.what_it_is: Eats objects whose surface traits are close to a remembered good item under the registered surface distance (PLACEHOLDER-91), and ignores core traits. C5's 'B2 lookup' is this bot, used there as a flat reference. Ledger X03.

baselines.name: Essence-trait matcher
baselines.what_it_is: Matches on the designer's core-trait list. It shows the test can be solved from one example and sets a ceiling. It is not a must-fail bot. Ledger X03.

baselines.name: Count-based novelty agent
baselines.what_it_is: A textbook curiosity agent with a visit-count novelty bonus. It must stay stuck on the glimmer stone, which proves the trap is real. Ledger X04.

baselines.name: Greedy eater
baselines.what_it_is: Moves to and eats the nearest object. Ledger X03.

baselines.name: Greedy eater plus proposal noise
baselines.what_it_is: B4 with Frankie's designed proposal noise added. It shows detours made by accident.

baselines.name: Oracle
baselines.what_it_is: Reads hidden natures and sets the ceiling. It lives only in the test-fixtures package. Ledger X03.

baselines.name: Contamination canary
baselines.what_it_is: Deliberately leaks vault kinds. T0 must flag it 100% of the time. Ledger X03.

baselines.name: Copycat
baselines.what_it_is: Copies the teacher from birth. After the teacher leaves, it eats kinds it saw the teacher eat, skips kinds it saw the teacher turn away from, and replays stored teacher motifs in matching situations. One frozen definition covers C9, C10 and C11. Ledger X06.

baselines.name: Hard-wired watcher
baselines.what_it_is: Writes 'what the teacher ate, then glowed, is good' straight into memory. Ledger X06.

baselines.name: Always-eat bot
baselines.what_it_is: Eats every object it meets. Gamer bot (X33).

baselines.name: Eat-novel-first bot
baselines.what_it_is: Goes for and eats never-tried things first. This is brute tasting. Gamer bot (X05).

baselines.name: Never-eat-new bot
baselines.what_it_is: Eats only kinds it has eaten before. Gamer bot (X33).

baselines.name: Reject-all-unknown bot
baselines.what_it_is: Refuses anything its memory does not recognise. Gamer bot (X05).

baselines.name: Avoid-the-familiar-look bot
baselines.what_it_is: Eats exact copies of h1 and anything that looks different from h1, and refuses near-copies. Gamer bot (X33).

baselines.name: Rarity-weighted matcher
baselines.what_it_is: Weights each trait by how unusual its value is in the bot's own experience, then matches to remembered eaten items. It is a matcher in C1 and a learner in C3, with one definition. If it passes, the vault is redesigned and the threshold is never touched. Gamer bot (X33).

baselines.name: Best single-trait bot
baselines.what_it_is: Uses the one trait that best predicted food in its own ancestral and lifetime experience (for example smell only). Gamer bot (X33).

baselines.name: Best two-trait bot
baselines.what_it_is: The same as G07, using the best pair of traits. Gamer bot (X33).

baselines.name: Scene-only bot
baselines.what_it_is: Eats in the home scene of kind F and refuses elsewhere. Gamer bot (X33).

baselines.name: Never-eat bot
baselines.what_it_is: Never eats. Gamer bot (X33).

baselines.name: Always-explore bot
baselines.what_it_is: Explores all the time, as much as possible. Gamer bot (X05).

baselines.name: Fixed-delay waiter bot
baselines.what_it_is: Waits a fixed time at any seed-shaped thing. Gamer bot (X05).

baselines.name: Nearest-known-food-else-random-walk bot
baselines.what_it_is: Goes to the nearest food it remembers, and does a random walk otherwise. Gamer bot (X05).

baselines.name: Failure-triggered explorer
baselines.what_it_is: A hard-wired rule, 'after a source fails, explore more', with no insurance reasoning. Built at Stage 4. Gamer bot (X33).

baselines.name: Fading-everything bot
baselines.what_it_is: Its sharp-look spending on every object declines with age. Built at Stage 4. Gamer bot (X33).

baselines.name: Flat tower
baselines.what_it_is: All recognition layers at once. There are two settings, logged in the version field: capped to Frankie's thinking spend, and zero thinking cost. Off-switch (X08).

baselines.name: No gating
baselines.what_it_is: Outer layers do not gate the inner ones. Off-switch (X08).

baselines.name: No objection
baselines.what_it_is: Inner layers cannot object (no inside-out reset). Off-switch (X08).

baselines.name: Gates forced to maximum
baselines.what_it_is: Context gates locked at full strength. Off-switch (X08).

baselines.name: Pick-the-max
baselines.what_it_is: The candidate with the most activation wins at once, with no competition. Off-switch (X08).

baselines.name: Prototype memory
baselines.what_it_is: Each kind is stored as one prototype in place of Frankie's memory format. Off-switch (X08).

baselines.name: Habits off
baselines.what_it_is: The habit rule (M34) is switched off. Off-switch (X35).

baselines.name: Write rule frozen
baselines.what_it_is: Memory is frozen and the write rule is off, with habits still on. C2's 'write-rule off-switch' and C3's 'frozen-memory version' are this one version. Off-switch (X35).

baselines.name: Always-split
baselines.what_it_is: The write rule always splits and never stretches. Off-switch (X35).

baselines.name: Taste-blind
baselines.what_it_is: Taste is removed from memory and from the verdict after eating. Off-switch (X35).

baselines.name: 'Unknown' unit off
baselines.what_it_is: The 'unknown' candidate cannot win. Off-switch (X35).

baselines.name: Sharp looks from proposals only
baselines.what_it_is: The value-of-information rule for sharp looks is off, so a sharp look happens only when a proposal makes it. Off-switch (X35).

baselines.name: Backups-don't-count (BDC)
baselines.what_it_is: The drive's estimate of what losing A would cost ignores every backup: remembered sources, and the expected value of untried things. Off-switch (X08).

baselines.name: FIXED-RANDOMNESS
baselines.what_it_is: The proposal count is held at one constant for every Frankie and tick: the designed curve's value at E = R+20 (2 under the current placeholder). Off-switch (X08).

baselines.name: NO-RICH-ARM
baselines.what_it_is: No extra randomness when rich: above R, the curve is held at its near-reserve value. Off-switch (X08).

baselines.name: Social path off (S clone)
baselines.what_it_is: The teacher is present but no social records are written. Perception is unchanged. Off-switch (X08).

baselines.name: Wrong-object social records (X clone)
baselines.what_it_is: Social records are written, but each one is linked to a randomly chosen other visible object. Off-switch (X35).

baselines.name: Trust locked at full
baselines.what_it_is: Follows every creature fully from the start. A test variant only, never part of Frankie: a test-only flag in the test-fixtures module, refused in any run labelled 'full'. Off-switch (X35).

baselines.name: Character off
baselines.what_it_is: Picks at random among the options considered, using the proposal stream. A test-only flag in the test-fixtures module, refused in any run labelled 'full'; the 'randomness never chooses' rule applies to version full only. Off-switch (X35).

baselines.name: Zero randomness
baselines.what_it_is: No proposals are drawn from randomness. Its stability must be exactly 1.0. Off-switch (X35).

baselines.name: Gating, objection and elimination off
baselines.what_it_is: C12's 'switched-off Frankie': tower gating, objection and tower elimination are all off, and randomness is unchanged. Off-switch (X35).

baselines.name: Hysteresis off (RETIRED)
baselines.what_it_is: Retired. No hysteresis exists in the main version (PLACEHOLDER-25, PLACEHOLDER-100), so this control switches off nothing. It is removed from X08 and C13 unless Aitzaz defines hysteresis before Stage 6.

baselines.name: Tower off, random choice among proposals
baselines.what_it_is: T15 control: the recognition tower's gating, objection and elimination are off, and the action is picked at random among the drawn proposals. A test-only flag, refused in any run labelled 'full'. Off-switch (X35). Replaces C12's claim-local 'random proposals without the tower'.

baselines.name: Exemplar twin (GCM style)
baselines.what_it_is: A textbook exemplar similarity learner (Nosofsky 1986, already cited in X07) with Frankie's own evolved weights and perception. Used by the credit rule. Conventional twin (X07).

baselines.name: Exemplar twin with an 'unknown' threshold
baselines.what_it_is: TW1 plus a threshold below which it answers 'unknown'. Conventional twin (X37).

baselines.name: Stretch-or-split write-rule twin
baselines.what_it_is: A conventional write rule that stretches or splits, with no outward blame. Conventional twin (M16).

baselines.name: Best-score chooser twin
baselines.what_it_is: The same drive, menu and randomness curve, but it takes the option with the highest predicted chance of staying above R (argmax) in place of the first acceptable one. Conventional twin (M30).

baselines.name: Epsilon-greedy twin
baselines.what_it_is: A best-score chooser with constant randomness, outside Frankie. Conventional twin (X07).

baselines.name: Payoff-biased social-learner twin
baselines.what_it_is: A textbook social learner that weights observed choices by their payoff. Conventional twin (X07).

baselines.name: Reliability-learning social twin
baselines.what_it_is: A textbook social learner that learns how reliable each demonstrator is. Conventional twin (X37).

baselines.name: Rate-based twin
baselines.what_it_is: The same mind with rate-based neurons in place of spiking ones. Reported only. Conventional twin (M43).

baselines.name: Serial-scan mock
baselines.what_it_is: A test fixture that searches every memory slot. It must fail C5 part (3). Test fixture (X34).

baselines.name: Positive-control accumulator mock
baselines.what_it_is: Reads hidden state and has the competition signature built in. It must pass C5 parts (1) to (5). Test fixture (X34).

baselines.name: Insurance mock (T7/T8)
baselines.what_it_is: A scripted cheat with insurance and a BDC switch built in. It must pass every part of C7 at Stage 4, and it drives the joint-power simulation. Test fixture (X34).

baselines.name: Patience mock (T9)
baselines.what_it_is: A scripted cheat with patience built in. It drives C8's joint-power simulation. Test fixture (X34).

baselines.name: Free-will mock (T14)
baselines.what_it_is: Scripted, with U-shaped dice and a habit rule built in. Test fixture (X34).

baselines.name: Strong copy-leak mock
baselines.what_it_is: Copies observed motifs with probability 0.3. It must be caught in at least 95% of pilots. Test fixture (X34).

baselines.name: Weak copy-leak mock
baselines.what_it_is: Its copy probability is tuned so that the expected wiggle share, A minus B, is 0.06. It must be caught in at least 80% of pilots. Test fixture (X34).

baselines.name: Social mock (G = 0.15)
baselines.what_it_is: Has a known watching gain of 0.15 and is used for C9's power check. Test fixture (X34).

baselines.name: Trust-slope mock
baselines.what_it_is: Has a known trust slope and is used for C10's power check. Test fixture (X34).

baselines.name: Hand-set (neutral) perception cohort
baselines.what_it_is: Frankies whose perception settings are hand-set to neutral in place of evolved. It separates what evolution supplied from what one life learned. Comparison cohort, not a bot.

baselines.name: Shuffled-world cohort
baselines.what_it_is: Frankies evolved in worlds whose essence rules were shuffled. Comparison cohort.

baselines.name: Counter-world cohort
baselines.what_it_is: Frankies evolved in worlds whose essence rules run against the test rule. Comparison cohort.

baselines.name: Kill-test Frankie tower
baselines.what_it_is: The bench-only spiking outside-in elimination tower with blame-outward memory and the bench drive. No body, movement or actions. Not v1 Frankie: the X01/X40/T17 exception covers K-F only, never v1 Frankie (KILL_TEST.md sections 1 and 12). Its tuned values may enter Frankie only as designed priors on the priors card (section 7).

baselines.name: K-F without warm-up
baselines.what_it_is: K-F run with no warm-up tastes. Reported only (KILL_TEST.md section 4).

baselines.name: Nearest-neighbour bot with a radius
baselines.what_it_is: B1n-bot that eats only if the nearest stored item is good and lies within a radius r chosen on the kill-test tuning set and frozen before any K-F code. One of the two kill-test floor minds, with B1n-mind; the floor is whichever has the higher mean D_learn on the set (KILL_TEST.md section 9, rule 3).

baselines.name: Inner-layer matcher
baselines.what_it_is: B1n-bot-r computed over parts and details traits only, with its own radius. Kill-test must-fail bot (KILL_TEST.md section 4).

baselines.name: Near-copy refuser
baselines.what_it_is: B1n-bot that, once a stored bad item lies within 10 noise widths of a stored good item over all observable traits, also refuses any object within 10 noise widths of some stored good item that is not an exact match of any stored good item. Kill-test must-fail bot (KILL_TEST.md section 4).

baselines.name: Inner-layer near-copy refuser
baselines.what_it_is: G16, with G16's radius, that also applies G17's trigger and near-copy refusal over all observable traits. Kill-test must-fail bot (KILL_TEST.md section 4).

baselines.name: Kill-test power-check mock
baselines.what_it_is: A test fixture that produces the planned values of every kill-test GO quantity, used only for the kill-test power check (KILL_TEST.md section 7, PLACEHOLDER-90).

log_fields.name: tick
log_fields.meaning: The basic row key: one row per creature per tick (PLACEHOLDER-64). Every claim's log uses it; no claim adds it separately.

log_fields.name: agent_id
log_fields.values: string, unique per tested life (Frankie or baseline)
log_fields.meaning: The one key for any tested agent. Replaces frankie_id and agent_id as separate names. World-side creatures, such as the teacher, use creature_id.

log_fields.name: agent_type
log_fields.values: frankie | K-F | K-F-NOWARM | a baseline id from the glossary (B0, B1t, B1n-bot, B1n-bot-r, B1n-forager, B1n-mind, B1n-seq, B2, B2e, B3, B4, B4n, B5, B6, B8, B9, G01-G18, TW1, TW1u, TW2-TW7, MK1-MK10)
log_fields.meaning: What kind of agent produced the row. A bare 'B1n' is not allowed.

log_fields.name: version
log_fields.values: full | OS01-OS21 | OS23 (OS22 retired); for OS01 also cap | free
log_fields.meaning: Which off-switch version of Frankie, if any.

log_fields.name: version_scope
log_fields.meaning: Whether the off-switch was applied on the same snapshot at test time or for the whole life.

log_fields.name: priors_cohort
log_fields.meaning: How the perception priors were produced.

log_fields.name: teacher_history
log_fields.meaning: Whether a teacher was ever present in this lineage of lives. The priors card checks it.

log_fields.name: matched_set_id / genome_id / temperament_seed / family_id / vault_id
log_fields.meaning: Matching and allocation keys (X38). Every claim uses exactly these names.

log_fields.name: snapshot_id / parent_snapshot_id / clone_id
log_fields.meaning: Snapshot lineage. C2's 'parent snapshot (T1)' is parent_snapshot_id.

log_fields.name: replica_key
log_fields.meaning: The replica index for the proposal and sensor-noise streams of this run. Replaces 'replica key', 'replica id' and 'replica'.

log_fields.name: stream_keys
log_fields.values: list of {stream: world | sensor | proposal | teacher, tick, creature, replica_key, draw_number}
log_fields.meaning: The full random-stream key record for every rerun (C13), including sensor-redraw keys.

log_fields.name: condition
log_fields.values: T1: O | Z | Z0. T2: PRE | SOUR | SWEET-CONTROL | MIRROR | MIRROR-CONTROL | H2-ONLY. T5: similar | dissimilar | high | low, with k. T6: NEW-SMELL | NO-SMELL | KNOWN-SMELL | NEW-SMELL-NO-NOVEL | NOVEL-GROUND. T7: experienced | naive. T8: CHANGE | NO-CHANGE | HUNGER-YOKED | TOPPED-UP. T9: SEED-EXPERIENCED | YOKED-FRUIT | NO-SEED crossed with HIGH | LOW. T15: A+B | A-only | B-only | neither | B1n-seq | random-proposals-no-tower (version OS23)
log_fields.meaning: The test condition, taken from the frozen spec. Replaces 'group', 'arm' and 'seed-history group'.

log_fields.name: pre_exposed
log_fields.meaning: T8 only: whether this life had the designed walk past B.

log_fields.name: clone_type
log_fields.values: T | N | S | X | Y (teacher tests C9, C10) ; wiggle-A | wiggle-B | wiggle-C (T12, replacing C11's A, B, C) ; FULL | BDC | FIXED-RANDOMNESS | NO-RICH-ARM | KNOWN-ONLY-B (T7, T8) ; STONE | STATIC (T9) ; probe ; redraw | sensor-redraw | energy-clamp | habit-undone | continuation-KEPT | continuation-REMOVED | continuation-FAST (T14) ; room (T13)
log_fields.meaning: Why this clone exists. Every value is unique across the battery.

log_fields.name: run_set
log_fields.meaning: C13-M5's three 10-run sets. Replaces C13's 'A, B or S', which clashed with C9's S clone.

log_fields.name: newborn_start
log_fields.meaning: Which newborn starting value (M25) the life used.

log_fields.name: E / R / b / desperation_slope
log_fields.values: E in whole milli-units; R in units; b in 0.1-0.6; slope in 0.05-0.3
log_fields.meaning: Energy, reserve, boldness and desperation slope, logged every tick.

log_fields.name: energy_band
log_fields.meaning: From the shared energy-band definition (E <= R-10 ; R-10 < E < R+20 ; E >= R+20). Used everywhere a band is named.

log_fields.name: fed
log_fields.meaning: E > R.

log_fields.name: action / movement_target
log_fields.values: an action from the body's action list, including turn direction; a cell or a world-side object id
log_fields.meaning: The action part of the tick's choice.

log_fields.name: gaze_target / gaze_distance / gaze_layer_reached
log_fields.values: world-side object or creature id (log only, never in the mind packet); cells; none | scene | object | parts | details
log_fields.meaning: The sharp-view part of the tick's choice.

log_fields.name: action_provenance
log_fields.meaning: Where the chosen action and its movement target came from. Steps that carry out a chosen target inherit its provenance. 'random proposal' becomes proposal. 'eliminated-by-prediction' is NOT a provenance value: a struck option is never the chosen action. designed-exposure marks an eat the harness forced. baseline-rule is for bots without Frankie's chooser.

log_fields.name: gaze_provenance
log_fields.meaning: Where the sharp-view target came from. 'drive' in C1, C6 and C9 becomes drive-sharp-look, which is valid only here.

log_fields.name: options_considered
log_fields.values: ordered list of {order, source: habit | proposal, option, predicted_p_above_R, cleared_bar: true | false}
log_fields.meaning: The satisficing chooser's pass over the options, in the order it considered them.

log_fields.name: satisficing_bar
log_fields.meaning: The required chance of staying above R this tick (0.9 - 0.3 x b under PLACEHOLDER-27) [Aitzaz Q3, 24 Oct].

log_fields.name: no_safe_option
log_fields.meaning: True when no option cleared the bar. The choice is then tagged no-safe-option-fallback (M47).

log_fields.name: struck_options
log_fields.values: list of struck-option events {option, source, target_object_id (world, log only), target_kind_id (world), predicted_p_above_R, strike_class: reasoned | rote | no-kind}
log_fields.meaning: Options the chooser ruled out by prediction before trying them. Each one is an event, never an action. strike_class follows the shared reasoned/rote rule. Replaces every 'eliminated-by-prediction' entry in provenance lists.

log_fields.name: proposal_count_target / proposals_drawn_count / proposal_draws
log_fields.values: real number before rounding; integer; list of {menu_entry, target, draw_number}
log_fields.meaning: The curve value, the whole number after stochastic rounding (PLACEHOLDER-96), and the draws.

log_fields.name: drive_trace_replayed
log_fields.values: per menu option: predicted_p_above_R, backup_contribution, order
log_fields.meaning: The exact-replay trace for testing (M53), including options the chooser never reached. Log only.

log_fields.name: decision_tick_type / margin_to_bar
log_fields.values: none | close-call | choice-change | both ; signed probability
log_fields.meaning: From the shared decision-tick definition, using delta from PLACEHOLDER-99.

log_fields.name: verdict_subject
log_fields.meaning: What the verdict was about, resolved by the harness (W53).

log_fields.name: verdict_winner / verdict_margin / settle_steps / verdict_scope
log_fields.values: candidate_id | unknown ; number ; integer ; full | blurry
log_fields.meaning: The committed verdict. Replaces 'winner'. blurry marks an outer-layer-only verdict (PLACEHOLDER-16).

log_fields.name: elimination_events
log_fields.meaning: Recognition-tower elimination among candidates ONLY. Never used for options the chooser struck (those go in struck_options).

log_fields.name: objection_events
log_fields.meaning: Inside-out objections.

log_fields.name: memory_write_events
log_fields.values: type: new | stretch | split | merge | mark-unreliable | forget ; trigger: chosen-eat | designed-exposure | watched ; candidate_id_before, candidate_id_after, layer, per-feature weight deltas
log_fields.meaning: Write-rule events. trigger=designed-exposure applies PLACEHOLDER-93.

log_fields.name: candidate_lineage
log_fields.values: rows of {parent_id, child_id, event: stretch | merge | split | forget}
log_fields.meaning: Log-side lineage (W53).

log_fields.name: eat_events
log_fields.values: {object_id, kind_id, hidden_nature (world-side scoring only), energy_delta, effect_tick, stomach_delay_d: 3 | 10, taste_vector, sick, net_gain, designed_exposure: true | false, cell}
log_fields.meaning: Every eat. stomach_delay_d records the delay actually applied. cell is the grid cell of the eat (own-eat-log cells, C7).

log_fields.name: designed_exposure
log_fields.meaning: Only for tests on the designed-exposure list. Printed on the priors card.

log_fields.name: injection_events
log_fields.values: type: energy-set | yoke-adjust | top-up | source-stop | source-resume | source-clear | object-place | object-remove | cue-inject | smell-mask ; tick, amount, vault provenance
log_fields.meaning: Every harness change to the world or to energy (W45). There is no survival-floor type, because the T13 survival floor is retired.

log_fields.name: probe_role
log_fields.values: far | lookalike | neutral | copy | U | member | filler | decoy | stickered | odd-detail | trust-test | never-shown-match | seed-probe | novel-probe
log_fields.meaning: World side only, never in the mind packet. novel-probe marks C8-S3's novel probe objects.

log_fields.name: trial_end_reason
log_fields.values: committed-eat | committed-skip | window-timeout | left-area | death | tick-cap | eat-cap
log_fields.meaning: One vocabulary for every trial and session.

log_fields.name: habit_weight_updates
log_fields.meaning: Replaces 'habit-table updates'. These are habit weights, not a value table, under the value-table boundary.

log_fields.name: habit_similarity_score / habit_similar / habit_contribution
log_fields.meaning: From PLACEHOLDER-98. habit_contribution=zero means no habit weight entered this choice.

log_fields.name: motif_tokens / tokenizer_fingerprint
log_fields.values: token strings under ledger X40 ; hash
log_fields.meaning: The one shared motif tokenizer.

log_fields.name: sign_condition / teacher_reliability_p / teacher_type
log_fields.values: visible | hidden | reversed | none ; 1.0 | 0.75 | 0.5 ; informative | uninformative
log_fields.meaning: 'signs normal' (C9) becomes visible. A 'signless' creature has sign_condition none.

log_fields.name: creature_id / creature_slot
log_fields.values: world-side id (log only) ; mind-side slot from creature tracking (PLACEHOLDER-39)
log_fields.meaning: Lets the log measure how often a slot resets for a creature that is still the same one.

log_fields.name: social_record_events
log_fields.values: {record_id, creature_slot, linked_candidate_id, trust_type: choice-trust | sign-meaning, influence_before, influence_after, substituted_object (X clones)}
log_fields.meaning: Mind-side social records.

log_fields.name: visit_events
log_fields.values: {spot: real-seed | dud-seed | reference-cell | stone | other, start_tick, end_tick}
log_fields.meaning: From the shared visit definition.

log_fields.name: room_reached / death_tick
log_fields.meaning: T13: whether the life reached room-entry age, and when it died.

log_fields.name: teacher_ever_present / teacher_demonstrations_seen

statistics_policy:
PRIMARY FAMILY (new ledger row X32). There are seven headline claims: C1, C2-SOUR, C3, C7, C8, C9 and C12, so m = 7 [Aitzaz Q4, 24 Oct]. Holm step-down at a familywise alpha of 0.05: sort the seven single p-values from smallest to largest and compare them in turn with 0.05/7 = 0.00714, 0.05/6 = 0.00833, 0.05/5 = 0.0100, 0.05/4 = 0.0125, 0.05/3 = 0.0167, 0.05/2 = 0.0250 and 0.05/1 = 0.0500. Reject in that order and stop at the first p that is above its level; that claim and every later one fail. If Aitzaz rules that taste never takes part in recognition, C2-SOUR leaves the family before the Wave 1 freeze and m = 6, giving levels 0.00833 to 0.05 [Aitzaz Q2, 24 Oct]. C4 may join only if its N is raised to 100 before the Wave 1 freeze, which makes m = 8 [Aitzaz Q4, 24 Oct]. Family membership and m are fixed at the Wave 1 freeze (X02), including C9 as a committed member even though C9 itself is frozen in Wave 2; Wave 2 may not add or remove members. If C2-SOUR leaves (m = 6) or C4 joins (m = 8), that also happens before the Wave 1 freeze. No document may hard-code a level such as '0.005' or 'at most 10 primaries'; every document cites X32. PLACEHOLDER-79 is closed by X32.

ONE RULE FOR EACH PRIMARY'S SINGLE p. A claim's Holm p is the largest one-sided p among its named effect parts. This is an intersection-union rule: because every effect part must pass, the false-positive rate cannot rise. The direction of every effect part is pre-registered. A part written as a confidence bound is converted into a one-sided p against its margin (non-inferiority or superiority). Any bound printed for an effect part is taken at the Holm level at which the claim is finally tested, never at a fixed 95%. The named effect parts are:
- C1: (2) D_beh(O) minus D_beh(Z), a one-sided permutation test stratified by family; and (4) FarMinusNeutral, a one-sided Wilcoxon. (4) loses its separate fixed 0.01.
- C2-SOUR: non-inferiority p-values for (1) mean Delta_far above -0.10, (2) Delta_far(SOUR) minus Delta_far(SWEET-CONTROL) above -0.10, and (3) mean Delta_look below +0.10.
- C3: the stratified log-rank one-sided p for E50, Frankie versus B1n-mind.
- C7: T7(1), T8(c) versus NO-CHANGE, and T8(c) versus HUNGER-YOKED.
- C8: S1; S6 seed versus dud; S6 seed versus the reference cell; S7 versus NO-SEED; S7 versus YOKED-FRUIT.
- C9: C9-M1, the one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank on G.
- C12: one-sided Mann-Whitney tests of R23 versus B0 and of R23 versus B1n-seq. Step 2 (R3) is a fixed-sequence follow-on: it is tested only if step 1 passes, at the level C12 received in Holm, with no extra alpha.

OTHER PARTS INSIDE A PRIMARY.
- Explanation gates are each tested at one-sided 0.05, uncorrected. Examples: C7's BDC, FIXED-RANDOMNESS and NO-RICH-ARM gates and T8(b1)/(b2); C8's S1b, S2, S3, S4 and S6b; C9-M2 to C9-M6; C12's hit-rate and switched-off comparisons; C3 (4). Gates decide what a pass is credited to or how it is labelled, never whether the effect exists.
- Floors are fixed thresholds on estimates (ratios, shares, minimum differences). They have no test and must hold.
- Validity, applicability and precondition checks are pass/void conditions. Where one needs a test, it uses one-sided 0.05.

ONE ALPHA FOR SECONDARY EVIDENCE. One secondary family of four members, Holm-corrected among themselves at a familywise 0.05 (levels 0.0125, 0.0167, 0.025, 0.05). Each member forms its single p with the same largest-p rule:
- C4: effect parts (a) versus no-objection, (b) versus no-gating, (d) e_in versus the flat tower, and (d) e_out versus gates forced to maximum.
- C6: effect parts (1) versus empirical chance, and (2) to (4), each under both responder and intention-to-treat scoring.
- C2-MIRROR: effect parts Delta_look below 0, and Delta_far non-inferiority at -0.15. A_look_post at most 0.30 and the MIRROR-CONTROL difference at most +0.10 are floors.
- C13-E (E1): effect parts KEPT versus REMOVED (Wilcoxon) and versus B1n-mind (Mann-Whitney).
This replaces C6's 0.01 and 0.05, MIRROR's 0.01 and E1's 0.005. Secondary results go in a separate table and are never merged into the headline tally. The optional T15 keeps its own Holm across its 5 controls at 0.05, outside both families.

MECHANISM CHECKS. C5, C10, C11, C13-M, C2-MEMORY, C4 (c), C8-S8 and every T0 check use one-sided 0.05 per test, unless the claim pre-registers a stricter level (C5 keeps its 0.01). A level is never looser than that, and these results are never counted as evidence. Two-sided tests are used only where no direction is pre-registered: differences from a twin, and 'not significantly below 0' checks. Crediting to a conventional twin uses each claim's stated 90% equivalence interval and sits outside every family. The cautious-start replicate is reported outside every family and is never a pass condition. PLACEHOLDER-80 is replaced: there is no two-sided default and no rank-biserial floor.

PART-LEVEL TAGS. In the charter table every part carries exactly one tag: PRIMARY-EFFECT, SECONDARY-EFFECT, GATE, FLOOR, VALIDITY, APPLICABILITY, MECHANISM or REPORTED. The claim-level tag is read off its effect parts. The mixed claims are tagged as follows:
- C2: SOUR (1) to (3) PRIMARY-EFFECT; SOUR (4) and the per-half means FLOOR; (5) APPLICABILITY; (6) REPORTED; (7) VALIDITY. MIRROR is SECONDARY-EFFECT, with the 30-room-Frankie rule as APPLICABILITY. MEMORY is MECHANISM.
- C4: (a), (b) and (d) SECONDARY-EFFECT; (c) MECHANISM; the bot profile VALIDITY.
- C8: S1, S6 and S7 PRIMARY-EFFECT; S1b, S2, S3, S4 and S6b GATE; S5 FLOOR; S8 MECHANISM; S9 VALIDITY.
- C13 is split into C13-M (M1 to M7, MECHANISM) and C13-E (E1, SECONDARY-EFFECT).
- C12: step 1 PRIMARY-EFFECT; step 2 PRIMARY-EFFECT (fixed sequence); H and switched-off GATE; rate-ratio 2 FLOOR; T15 REPORTED (optional, own family).
- Twin crediting: in every claim (C1, C2, C3, C4, C6, C7, C9, C10, C12, C13-E) the twin-crediting part is tagged GATE and sits outside every family. It uses the claim's 90% equivalence interval and stated margin; a two-sided difference p, where computed, is REPORTED only.
A claim counts in the evidence tally only through its PRIMARY-EFFECT or SECONDARY-EFFECT parts. N comes from the joint-power rule (X39), may only go up, and is never changed after results are seen.

The level each primary claim is tested at, under ledger X32 (m = 7; strictest step 0.05/7, about 0.0071). Secondary evidence uses its own family of 4 at a familywise 0.05. The full rule is in the statistics policy. The literal values '0.005' and '10 primaries' are retired.

well-below: E <= R-10. near: R-10 < E < R+20. well-above: E >= R+20. These are C7's bands, frozen in the Stage 4 specs as new ledger row M54. They are the only bands used anywhere: C7, C13, habit similarity (PLACEHOLDER-98) and log field energy_band.

The bar is the predicted chance of staying above R over the drive horizon that an option must reach. One rule: boldness lowers the bar, with required chance = 0.9 - 0.3 x b (PLACEHOLDER-27) [Aitzaz Q3, 24 Oct]. PLACEHOLDER-22 is restated as 'the bar comes from PLACEHOLDER-27'. Boldness does not reweight losses. C13 and C7's boldness split cite this rule and no other role.

The habit option is considered first, then proposals in the order drawn (PLACEHOLDER-23) [Aitzaz Q3, 24 Oct]. If no option clears the bar, Frankie takes the option with the best chance of staying above R (ledger M47) [Aitzaz Q3, 24 Oct]. That choice is tagged action_provenance=no-safe-option-fallback with no_safe_option=true, and its share is reported (C7). This is the only place a best-score rule is allowed inside Frankie. The backups-don't-count gate covers it.

A sampled tick for C13 is one of two types. Type close-call: an option ahead of the chosen one in the chooser's order missed the bar by less than delta, or the chosen option cleared the bar by less than delta. On a no-safe-option tick, where the fallback is a best-score rule, close-call means another option is within delta of the fallback's chance. Type choice-change: the choice differs from the previous tick's. delta = 0.05 in predicted chance of staying above R (PLACEHOLDER-99). Margins come from the replayed drive trace (M53). PLACEHOLDER-67 ('top two options within 0.05') is retired.

shared_definitions.term: Proposal-count curve, N_max and fractional counts
shared_definitions.definition: Above and near R, PLACEHOLDER-25 is unchanged: 1 proposal within 10 units of R, rising in a straight line to 4 at R+40. Below R-10 the count rises at that Frankie's own desperation slope s (PLACEHOLDER-26): count = 1 + s x (R-10-E), capped at N_max = 6 (PLACEHOLDER-97). The FIXED-RANDOMNESS value is the curve at R+20, which is 2 under the placeholder, and is unaffected. A fractional count x is rounded stochastically: floor(x)+1 with probability equal to the fractional part, drawn from the proposal stream (PLACEHOLDER-96). So a T14 redraw also redraws the rounding.

There is none in the main version (PLACEHOLDER-25, PLACEHOLDER-100). The hysteresis-off control (OS22) and the 'hysteresis state' log field are removed from X08 and C13. If Aitzaz defines hysteresis before Stage 6, it gets a ledger row and C13's conditional pass rules come back.

The similarity score counts how many of three parts match between a situation and a habit origin: scene, top recognised kind in view, and energy band (M54). It runs from 0 to 3. 'Similar' means 3/3, and C13's 'window threshold' is 3 (PLACEHOLDER-98, which replaces PLACEHOLDER-29). Habit contribution is 'zero' when no habit weight entered the choice. C13-M3 and C13-E1 use exactly these terms.

A struck option is an option the chooser ruled out by prediction before trying it. It is logged as a struck-option event in struck_options and never as an action or a provenance value. shared_definitions.term: Value table (boundary of the forbidden entry)
shared_definitions.definition: Allowed: tallies (counts or sums of energy changes) of Frankie's OWN outcomes for a situation or option. Each tally is updated only from outcomes seen within a fixed credit window after that choice, with no discounting, and is never updated from another estimate. This covers M34's habit weights (logged as habit_weight_updates), PLACEHOLDER-21's counting estimator, and the trust and influence updates of PLACEHOLDER-40 and PLACEHOLDER-41, whose credit window is 300 ticks after the watched event (Claude placeholder). Banned: anything that updates one situation's value from another situation's value or estimate, including TD errors, Bellman backups, discount factors, Q-tables, value functions and eligibility traces that pass value backward across situations. Review checks the habit and drive design notes against this line. Aitzaz confirms it at initialling.

shared_definitions.term: Boredom counter (boundary of the forbidden entry)
shared_definitions.definition: Forbidden: any quantity, per object, per kind, per place or cell, or global, that grows or shrinks with the number of looks, visits or exposures whatever their outcome. This includes a per-place look count for an object that never moves. Allowed: fading place-and-time records, each tied to an observed outcome ('investigated here, nothing came of it'), and these records may add up [Aitzaz Q2, 24 Oct]. T0(e) code check: run scripted repeated looks with the outcome-record write intercepted. Any mind state that still changes with the number of looks, apart from the sensory buffer, flags a counter. PLACEHOLDER-109 holds the rule.
